# Squirrel package and installed-version identity

Run the exact root entrypoint `build-installer.bat /s`. It builds the real desktop payload and produces unsigned Squirrel.Windows `Setup.exe`, `RELEASES`, and `MaterialBuildroot-<version>-full.nupkg`. The output receipt binds the files to the unchanged source commit, tree, index, manifest, lockfile, and effective installed version. Packaging checks the actual application archive metadata against that version. Production does not install or launch the application and does not establish update, rollback, or runtime acceptance.

Every normal installer production calls `assemblePayloads` with `complete: true` and packages the complete declared tool inventory through `extraResources`. The real installed consumer already resolves `resources/offline-payloads/manifest.json` before user-selected tool receipts, with original companion files and notices retained. The package producer requires the assembled manifest hash and notice file in the unpacked package, and records complete inventory/source/license metadata in the source-bound receipt. A directory development build remains explicitly core-only and does not claim bundled-tool completeness.

Use `--payload-cache <absolute-directory>` to reuse previously acquired immutable archives. Only registry-named archive files are copied into the producer's own ignored cache. Source caches remain read only, and assembly revalidates every pinned archive before extraction. No absolute cache path enters publication metadata. Each produced release asset is measured and must fit the 1.4 GB transfer budget; oversized output is retained as incomplete production rather than being renamed or misrepresented.

Installer production uses an exclusively created short directory under the current writable temporary directory because the genuine NuGet packaging tool retains legacy path-length limits. A private ownership receipt records source and ownership there; its path and receipt are excluded from public output. The producer checks the deepest assembled path against its packaging budget before launching NuGet. Failed staging is retained. Activation still verifies the complete source-bound output; a cross-volume activation copies the verified output while retaining the original producer tree. This changes no host path-limit setting and substitutes no packaging tool.

## Native broker resource

Normal desktop installer production initializes the verified installed MSVC x64 and Windows SDK route through the root entrypoint, then calls `scripts/build/native-file-broker.ps1` inside the same source-bound production. The generated executable and its matching SHA-256 manifest are appended as `resources/native-file-broker/material-file-broker.exe` and `resources/native-file-broker/broker-manifest.json`, alongside the complete offline tool resource. The object file is not packaged. The producer checks the compiled identity again after packaging and records only toolchain versions and hashes, without compiler or machine paths.

A missing supported installed compiler or SDK stops the root entrypoint honestly. This path performs no local toolchain installation, license acceptance, elevation, or host setting change. Hosted production can use its verified existing compiler installation. A compiled broker remains `runtimeVerified: false`; packaging alone does not admit external adapters or establish isolation, cancellation, or output-publication runtime acceptance. Development directory builds remain explicitly without a produced broker unless a separate supported production supplies one.

## Genuine setup embedding and admission

The genuine helper source is retained unchanged in `native/squirrel-writezip/`, with its original MIT notice and byte/hash provenance from official Squirrel.Windows revision `eef37460aef77b2f9de8cd2237c1e55b344a6554` (tag `2.0.1`). The root producer compiles that source for x64 using the same verified installed compiler route. Through the supported `customSquirrelVendorDir` option it copies the pinned genuine vendor inventory and substitutes only the rebuilt `WriteZipToSetup.exe`. It does not introduce a custom self-extracting format, patch an executable, alter the setup template, or claim a compiler result as installation proof.

This route addresses a concrete packaging boundary: the pinned vendor helper is a 32-bit executable without large-address awareness, while its official source reads the entire embedded ZIP into memory before the resource update. The retained large-payload run produced a setup containing only its template updater. The official `2.0.1` source logs and continues after an embedding-helper failure. The original helper's exact failure and any before/after resource-edit transition were not captured, so an address-space limit remains a hypothesis rather than a proven cause. A successful future x64 production must establish the actual embedding outcome.

Before production can succeed, `squirrel-setup.cjs` reads the actual configured setup's PE resource tree and embedded ZIP directory. It requires the exact current full-package filename, a single-record `RELEASES`, and the genuine updater, rejects missing, duplicate, encrypted, escaping or unsupported members, and streams the embedded contents to compare sizes and SHA-256 identities. The embedded feed's SHA-1 and size must match that same full package. The resulting receipt records member identities and byte counts without machine paths. An `MZ` signature or filename alone never establishes a complete offline installer. Post-packaging resource editing remains enabled; preservation of the complete payload must pass actual admission.

The retained complete-payload run from source `bd0a4fce58cc69cd9ec19b30ba86a9ec7d166720` assembled ten tools, 30,972 files and 3,760,387,226 uncompressed bytes, then produced a 1,450,598,556-byte full package and 1,392,019,114-byte delta. Its root entrypoint exited `1` because the full package exceeded the unchanged 1.4 GB budget. Its 228,864-byte configured setup embedded only a 35,682-byte ZIP containing a 69,120-byte template updater, with no full package or feed. The output was retained and never activated or published. That run is failure evidence, not complete offline installer acceptance. The new x64 helper, embedding admission, native broker production and any subsequent size repair remain unverified until their actual source-bound production runs.

## Release versions

`MATERIAL_BUILD_VERSION` selects an explicit three-component numeric version. Otherwise a hosted `GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER` selects `<source major>.<source minor>.<run number>`. Components are bounded to 0 through 65534, and a workflow sequence is positive. Each independently numbered hosted build therefore changes the actual installed application and Squirrel package version, rather than merely changing a release tag while shipping version 0.1.0 again. Retrying the same workflow run retains its installed version. The release provenance and tag use the receipt's exact package version, and publication rejects a conflicting build/publication identity.

A local build without either input uses the source manifest version and records `packageVersionSource: local-base`. This is suitable for local production only. Manual publication requires an explicit `MATERIAL_BUILD_VERSION`, chosen strictly newer than the published installed version; publishing a locally produced base version is rejected. Keep the same version input for production and publication. Do not rewrite historical release tags or replace their packages.

## Genuine delta production

Set `MATERIAL_BUILD_SQUIRREL_BASELINE` to a local directory containing a previous release's `RELEASES` and its matching full package before invoking the root installer entrypoint. Acquire those files through the project's existing trusted release route. The producer preserves the originals, rejects linked baseline paths, bounds metadata and package size, selects the newest strictly older compatible full package, and verifies its SHA-1 and byte count against `RELEASES`. This is transport integrity, not a publisher authenticity claim.

Hosted installer production automatically acquires a baseline when no explicit local baseline is supplied. The exact root driver uses the previously bootstrapped GitHub CLI to discover at most thirty normal releases, select an older numeric version, download its provenance, verify the exact peeled tag/source identity and compatible package version, then acquire only `RELEASES` and that version's full package. Asset byte counts and SHA-256 values must match the release API and provenance; the subsequent Squirrel staging also checks the feed's SHA-1. Metadata is capped at 1 MiB per file and the full package at 1.5 GB. The ignored cache preserves inputs, permits at most eight acquisition directories, and stops at the bound rather than deleting evidence. Baseline readback or integrity failures stop production; an inventory with no eligible older release records delta unavailable explicitly. Receipts retain the baseline tag/source, package identity and hashes without local paths. There is no separate workflow-only packaging command that bypasses this root producer.

The verified baseline is copied into the isolated Squirrel output directory. The pinned genuine Squirrel releasifier produces the new full and delta packages. A supplied baseline without a resulting delta fails production. Generated `RELEASES` entries must match each package's actual bytes and digest. The output keeps the older full package needed by that feed alongside the current packages. Publication must retain every package named by the feed.

Without a baseline the producer creates a valid full-package release and records `delta.status: unavailable` with its reason. It never fabricates a delta or treats that state as two-version update proof. To produce the next delta, provide the previous successful output's Squirrel directory or the corresponding downloaded release files, and choose a strictly higher installed version.

## Scope and remaining evidence

No paid certificate or public trust claim is introduced. Unsigned packages can trigger unknown-publisher or SmartScreen warnings. Installation, installed launch, cross-version update, cancellation, rollback, and native runtime behavior require separate acceptance evidence. Under the fast release workflow, tests, reviews, static analysis, screenshots, installation, and runtime checks are intentionally not run. PH10-T02 remains pending its final applicable acceptance until those separately required records exist.
